# ROC curves

Receiver operating characteristic curves for one or more numeric
predictors of a binary outcome, with the area under each curve (AUC),
its DeLong 95% confidence interval (when pROC is installed), and the
Youden-optimal cut-off. The curves and AUCs are computed in the package
and match [`pROC::roc()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/pROC/man/roc.html); the
AUC is the Mann-Whitney estimate, so ties count one half.

## Usage

``` r
rocCurve(
  data,
  response,
  predictors,
  positive = NULL,
  direction = "auto",
  ci = TRUE,
  show.youden = TRUE,
  colors = NULL,
  main = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

- data:

  A data frame.

- response:

  The binary outcome column (two distinct values).

- predictors:

  Numeric predictor columns.

- positive:

  The level of `response` that is a case. Default: the second factor
  level, `TRUE`, `1`, or the larger of two values.

- direction:

  `"auto"`, `"<"` (cases have higher values) or `">"` (cases have lower
  values). `"auto"` compares the medians, as pROC does.

- ci:

  Logical; compute the DeLong confidence interval (needs pROC).

- show.youden:

  Logical; mark each curve's Youden-optimal cut-off.

- colors:

  Named vector of colours for the predictors.

- main:

  Optional plot title.

## Value

A `plotly` object, with the per-predictor table (AUC, CI, direction,
Youden cut-off, sensitivity and specificity there, cases and controls)
as attribute `"table"`.

## See also

[`rocCurveServer()`](https://j-andrews7.github.io/sciVizModules/reference/rocCurveServer.md),
[`pROC::roc()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/pROC/man/roc.html)

## Author

Jared Andrews

## Examples

``` r
data(example_biomarkers)
rocCurve(example_biomarkers, response = "disease",
    predictors = c("marker_strong", "marker_moderate", "marker_weak"))
```
